utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, the Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to you as well, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like to remind you, you are still bound by the solemn declaration that you have given at the beginning of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, are you ready to continue your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, we are now going to turn to the issue of the terrain, hygiene, and sanitation measures. Pages 245, 246, and 262 in your report. The first document I'd like to call up is 2D070167. And this is a document dated the 15th of October, 1993. It's authored by Dr. Brkic from the health care administration and veterinary department and is issued from the Ministry of Defence, and we can see the first page there. "Guidance on hygiene and sanitation measures applying to the terrain under control of Croatian army units." And as I said, author by the health care administration chief, Colonel Brkic. Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you aware that Dr. Brkic was described as the health care administration chief working out of the Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably knew before coming to the ICTY, but during my work here I have not come across information in relation to Dr. Brkic and his occupations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Shall we turn to page 2 of the report. As we can see, the preliminary opening's on page 1. And his guidance here goes through the various natures of the type of work that has to be done. We can see finding identification and the burial of killed enemy troops and civilians, eliminating animal corpses, wandering cattle being taken care of, and various other related steps. In the second to last paragraph, it is written: "Hygiene and sanitation measures are performed by the regional Civilian Protection Staff in cooperation with units that require hygiene and sanitation ..." and it depends on the scale of the operation. We have no need to go further through this report which speaks to itself in a very obvious way as to the kind of measures to be taken, but it's relevant because it is a guidance that is stated -- that is cited by the chief of staff, General Cervenko. Do you recollect that he refers to 1993 guidance?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no specific recollection that the chief of the Main Staff, General Cervenko, refers to this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the information does not need to be gone into further detail, but I ask that it be an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1056.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1056 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Let us turn now, then, to the measures taken and what was written at the time concerning this matter, because it is one of the features that you point out in relation to your conclusion that General Cermak, on a daily basis, issues orders and takes measures aimed at normalising life, and while doing so, is the most senior authority in Knin and superior to the civilian police and MP, military police, in Knin. So let us look at the first document, D -- Exhibit D598. On the 5th of August, 1995, this order was issued by General Cervenko, and it's an order concerning sanitization of the territory in which Operation Storm is conducted. First of all, is this a document you're familiar with?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, because I have in the section discussing Operation Storm, i.e., the day-by-day development during and after storm, I have included an order by General Gotovina to establish sanitation teams within the zone of responsibility of the Split Military District, and I remember -- or I seem to remember that he refers to an order from the chief of the Main Staff which may well be this specific document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. That is an order that was issued on the 11th of August of 1995, Exhibit P496 for reference purposes. We can see here that the chief of staff is issuing orders to the military districts, including Split, about establishing a mixed sanitization detachment. We can see there the types of matters which are obvious to that. If we turn to page 2, we can see units mentioned at the top. We can see that the sanitization teams invariably include criminal investigation technicians from the MUP for identification, persons for keeping records, medical team for immediate medical assistance, explosives experts, pathologist, or other physician trained to establish causes of death, utility company employees for funerals, and vets. And then in 2 we can see in coordination with the police administrations and Health Crisis staff in counties, they are to include a civilian protection unit from the county police administration in those particular districts there, and that does not mention Split ZP in paragraph 2. In the course of the work of the sanitization detachment the commander shall coordinate all issues.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think in paragraph 2 the first section applies to all the military districts, and then in the Bjelovar, Karlovac and Gospic military district and other special, what is called DDD squad, has to be included. But my impression is that the first part of the sentence applies to all the military districts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. If we turn to page 3, because we find here the reference to that report that we've just looked at, because 3 says that it shall be conducted in accordance with the instructions of the order of the health administration, 15th of October, 1993. We can see the points that are being made there, and the order goes on to deal with those issues, and the end of the order on page 5 was sent to the Split Military District. So we know, then, Mr. Theunens that the senior military authorities were taking steps from the 5th of August in relation to hygiene and sanitation of the terrain and issuing instructions which showed coordination between both civil and military authorities; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. And just for your information, General Gotovina's order can be found on English page 147 of the second part of the report. What I found interesting in the context of the order by General Gotovina is that he also establishes a team for Knin, but there is no reference in his order to the garrison commander in Knin, even though General Gotovina's order dates from the 11th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And that is right. And we are going through all the steps taken to get to the 11th of August, because the documents in between need to be looked at, Mr. Theunens. The next document is Exhibit P506, and it's that order now we can look at dated 5th of August that you've referred to on a number of occasions as being an order issued on that date, as you said, to show that Mr. Cermak was in authority on that date. Your footnote 976. We see Exhibit P506 now. It was issued by General Cermak, and it has that date the 5th of August. Now, I gathered from remarks you made yesterday that you've actually considered the issue of that date as I flagged it up with you as something that needed to be analysed.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. The numbering, when you look at later orders by General Cermak for the -- I mean issued during the following days, they have a lower file number. They may have 08, 07 at the end instead of 10. Now, there are different options. I cannot draw a final conclusion. It could be that the date is incorrect. It could be that the number is incorrect. It could be that both are incorrect. But what is interesting also is there is no reference to the order of General Cervenko. In the introduction it's not obligatory to have that reference, but it's quite common to do so, and there is no reference to the order of General Gotovina. Again one cannot draw a final conclusion on -- on that because, okay, one could say, Well, the fact that there's no reference to these other orders means that this order may have been issued prior to the other orders, but I'm not going to draw the conclusion, because it could also be that General Cermak considered it not necessary to refer to these other orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We know that an Exhibit D609 ends with that classification, that number 3231, which is the military stamp. 019509, and D609 is dated the 10th of August, but this ends in a 10 and is dated the 5th of August. Is that something that your research, because I know you've looked at the numbers confirms?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. D609 has the number 09 at the end. However, I have also recollection that, for example, in footnote 982 there is a document ending in 02, which is dated the 8th of August. The number 10, I mean ending 10, I have found it also on, I believe, one other occasion but much later. So as I said earlier, it could be indeed that the date is wrong, but it could also be that the number is wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You've told us that already.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No need to repeat it. But we will look further at Dr. Brkic. But in terms of what happened, Mr. Cermak himself had not arrived in Knin on the 5th of August. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that on the 5th of August he was appointed to his position.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That's not the question. Did you know whether he had arrived in Knin on the 5th of August or not?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know whether he had arrived on the 5th of August or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There is evidence in the case that he arrived on the 6th of August, and that is a matter that can be flagged up now. We see there the terms of the order. We have no need to look any further at it. Let us now go to Exhibit D603. This is a 65 ter, 4956, Mr. Theunens. It's a special report to the deputy minister, and it comes from the chief of the Civilian Protection Department in Zagreb, Mr. Cemerin. Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I came across that document while conducting research.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you cite it within your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. And I believe it covers the entire territory of Croatia, i.e., the territory that was -- over which Croatian control was restored as a result of Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The Civilian Protection Department is within the Ministry of Interior and the organisation responsible for the hygiene and sanitation of the terrain within the Ministry of Interior; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. We can see here that on the 4th of August, the chief of the sector informs the deputy minister that civilian protection units were prepared pursuant to an order for activation, Zadar-Knin police administrations. We'll be looking at that later, and says that it is necessary to proceed in the police administrations to the clearance of the dead from the terrain in the area liberated in coordination with the military authorities and with their approval coordinating with the crime police. The same telegram required these police administrations to participate in logistical support for organisation of collection centres. If we turn now to the next page, having seen that on the 5th of August, at the bottom there, that is the dateline, but on page 2, if we can go up to the top of the page, we're missing a bit, 1910 hours the deputy minister announced our units were entering, amongst the places Knin, and at 1917 hours Dr. Brkic called and announced he and his people were going first in accordance with the agreement with vice-president Kostovic and we are to prepare units for clearance which should be clearing up the area in question from the morning of the 6th of August onwards. Do you know about the agreement with the Vice-president Kostovic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the agreement between Mr. Brkic and --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Or an agreement in which Mr. Brkic was following an agreement with Vice-president Kostovic? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not specifically, but I would see it more in a sense of an authorisation by Kostovic in that sense, but anyway it comes back to the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We can see at that talks were being held with the police administrations including Zadar Knin on preparing units on that day. A telegram was sent, order on conducting clearance with detailed instructions on the method of conducting clearance and a sample form which should be completed with data on those killed. Zadar Knin police administration was sent assistance for carrying out the clearance tasks, and we see the numbers of people that were added to the team. And then we go down to the 6th of August. We can see that Messers Batur, Zadar-Knin police administration who is the chief of the civilian protection department of that body, and others, were sought brief instructions regarding clearing roads and approaches to liberated settlements. And a meeting was held at 9.55 with the Crisis Health Staff including Mr. Cemerin who wrote this document. Would you agree that that shows an organised approach to this matter being conducted through the Ministry of Interior concerning the sanitation of the terrain?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. And it reminds me a bit of what we discussed in the context of military command and control with the professional line. Procedures are established by the Ministry of Interior as to how to do it, and as we saw on the first page, the actual clearing is conducted in coordination and with the authorisation of the military authorities in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. If we turn to the next page. We see further details of what unfolds during that a day concerning the actions taken. We've no need to look at them any further. It is information about the process. In page 4, if we move to that, we see no information had been received from Sibenik police administration regarding clearance of Drnis, and then in bold the following problems were observed over the course of the day: Units left to their own devices largely in operations, without necessary equipment, poor communications, Zadar-Knin police administration hindered because of the extent of the liberated territory, coordination within each police administration unsatisfactory. And owing to the above, we see a man here, Mr. Boris Davidovic, being sent from the Ministry of Interior department to the territory of Zadar-Knin as coordinator for the conduct of clearance in the police administration's territory. Just stopping there and looking at Mr. Davidovic, is that a name that you recognise from the information that you were looking at concerning this issue?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may have seen the name before, but I have not mentioned him in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. First down we see again further steps taken including those by Mr. Davidovic. Page 5 --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just want to highlight that the text in bold applies to the, as I see the document now, the entire territory where Operation Storm was conducted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We've worked that out, yes.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Page 5. Further information about what is happening. Again going through what was required in Knin, the steps taken. Moving as well to the 7th of August date before this report was written. And then on the 8th of August various other steps. Let us turn to page 6. Those steps on the 8th, in the third paragraph, Mr. Davidovic, at 2050 hours, reporting, and a report from Mr. Cicko who was yesterday appointed the coordinator of the clearance of Knin, who reported at 2200 hours on the 8th of August the situation in Knin regarding organisation is extremely poor. There were 170 members of the civil protection working in Knin that day. And then going into the details of that, strenuous physical labour, the temperature. Zadar-Knin police administration operatives have not shown the slightest interest in providing logistical support. Mechanical digger is out of order and immobilised. You can see the detail there. And then Dr. Brkic appears. This is at page 5 in the Croatian-language document. About 20 bodies were picked up today in Knin, stored in refrigeration until burial. Dr. Brkic is causing certain problems. So Cicko asked for his activity to be restricted. Until Mr. Cicko arrived, the burials organised by the Zadar-Knin police administration, and he says by agreement with Dr. Brkic, were in a common grave. A particular problem is the lack of any communications out of Knin at all, so that today it was not even possible to establish communications from General Cermak's command. And we see the further detail there. The last page is just the signing by Mr. Cemerin of this -- this document. Having pointed out those matters, would you agree it shows that, first of all, the Ministry of Interior, even till this time, had set up a programme for dealing with the hygiene and sanitation in the terrain?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and it's being implemented, as we saw on the first page, in coordination and with the authorisation of the military authorities in the area. Can I just say something about --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- Dr. Brkic and the common grave?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have a report by --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We're going through all the -- please, if you just follow me. I don't want you to make speeches --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I don't think, as a matter of fact, that Mr. Theunens was preparing for making a speech.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the same time, if you would follow the line of questioning developed by Mr. Kay, and if anything you think might be missing then at the end you'll have an opportunity to supplement whatever was missing. So if there's a certain matter you would like to raise, please make a short note and then check at the end whether everything has been covered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I thank Your Honour, and I wasn't being rude, Mr. Theunens. It's just that I do have a programme and a time limit, and I want to make sure things are covered in a progressional way. Your Honour, may this document be made an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I thought it was already an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. I was taken out of my stride there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again, other than that reference to General Cermak there, no other reference to him at all and no reference to him as being coordinating or in charge of those measures being taken by the civil protection department. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right, but I want to point out that the report discusses the situation throughout the area covered by Operation Storm, and on the other hand, as we just saw, the fact that it was not possible to establish communications from -- with General Cermak's command is highlighted in the report, which means that it is important for the implementation of the sanitation tasks to have communication with General Cermak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It says: "A particular problem is the lack of any communications out of Knin at all ..." so out of Knin at all, "so that today it was not even possible to establish communications ..." which does not apply essentially to solely General Cermak but to communicating with anyone in Knin; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, that is correct, but the fact that General Cermak is -- his name is highlighted in the report, to me, means something, because there are many more people in Knin, obviously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It may be clear that -- it seems that the general situation is described and specific mention is made that no communication with General Cermak's command could be established, which means that at least that has been on their minds, and it may even have been attempted to do so. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we now turn to 65 ter 5387. Footnote 976 in your report. And we see here -- I don't have a date on this document in the English, but on the Croatian language we can see the 8th of August date, and it's from Dr. Brkic. It's to General Cermak, and it's a report about hygiene and sanitation measures, and it refers --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it true that the English document does not correspond in any way with the original, what we see on our screen at the moment? I've never seen a translation which takes approximately four times the size --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. There's obviously been something there that's happened in the system, Your Honour, and from my perch here I can now see the full text. Yeah. If we can just look at the English version in the interests of time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is a report from Brkic to General Cermak referring to the order, referring to the instructions we've looked at from 1993 and giving details of various dates, 7th of August, 8th of August, 9th of August, of people who had been processed, and remarking that all have been processed in accordance with the provisions of the Geneva Convention and buried as usual. Graves have been marked with regular intervals, and crosses with a mark have been put on each of them. And all unidentified persons in a process of secondary identification, and another report to be filed during the day. There are further reports we will look at, so we'll just go through them so that they are -- are dealt with, but there apparently is a conflict between Mr. Brkic, Brigadier Brkic, and Mr. Cemerin concerning who had done what correctly, we can point out from this document. May this document be made an exhibit, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me first clarify the issue. I mean, if it's admitted into evidence, then, of course, it will be the original and the translation. I noticed that the ERN of the English translation ends with 7670, whereas it appears that the original we find now on our screen the last four digits are 7667.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's a certification page at the back which we're not looking at for obvious -- unless Your Honour wants to certify it's a copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I just want to know for sure that when we admit something in evidence that we know what we are admitting, and I'll have a --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Page 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I don't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I have on my screen under this number is, as you said before, the document dated the 8th of August, 1995, whereas the English translation is not only longer but also without a date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's not the same document. It's not the same document, yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. But if we admit something in evidence, we have to take together the original and the translation, and therefore a final decision on admission should wait until we have seen the original properly uploaded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'll ask the Prosecution to supply the original. It's not an uploaded by us, so we will get it sorted out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not blaming anyone, but I'm not very much inclined to admit into evidence the translation of a document which is a totally different document. That's --

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: We'll try to find the original B/C/S that corresponds with the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and once you have found it, once you have uploaded it, can you inform us so we can decide on the matter, but it could already be marked for identification awaiting the uploaded of the original. Mr. Registrar, that would be --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit number 1057, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The next document is Exhibit D609, footnote 977 or 1048, concerning the order by General Cermak to Dr. Brkic for the disposal of -- of refuse. We put that in for completeness. D6 -- we'll move on from there. Exhibit D610 is a further order concerning animal hygiene and sanitation measures. There's no need to call that up. And we can now move to 2D07-0423. This document is also dated the 10th of August, 1995, and it's a request for the transfer of personnel from the Civil Defence, and it says in regard to the sanitation of the municipality of Knin: "We request the transfer of personnel from the Ministry of Interior, city of Zagreb, to the staff for the sanitation for the terrain in Knin with the aim of improving efficiency." And it's a request for Mr. Cicko who had been mentioned in that earlier report, the Court will recollect, and a Dr. Santetic is also mentioned, and asking for them to be placed with the Knin garrison temporary, and it's signed by General Cermak. So indicating there, Mr. Theunens, wouldn't you agree that Mr. Cermak wasn't ordering the Civil Defence in the Ministry of Interior but requesting assistance in relation to these measures?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. And it shows that a distinction has to be made between the authority of General Cermak in Knin, and then as we also saw yesterday with the documents for military personnel, he requested from various structures, so the distinction between the authority in Knin and his position towards the outside world where obviously a garrison commander or somebody in the position of General Cermak in the city of Knin cannot order somebody in a ministry in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And we know from that earlier report by Mr. Cemerin, dated the 8th of August, that, in fact, Mr. Cicko was already down there and working.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that's possible. I don't remember exactly, but it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, it was important because he was the person who was critical about Dr. Brkic, if you remember in the passage that I read out to you.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, may this document be made an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it was. Wasn't it D610?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, this is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes. We have no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number D1058.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1058 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Theunens, we saw the other document. I think it was D609, footnote 977. From what I remember, there was -- one of the terms used there was "subordination." Do you remember that? And in view of the last questions, could you explain the situation as far as requesting for the assistance, subordination to clarify how we exactly would have to understand that. Perhaps we could have it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Exhibit D609.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the distinction between the two documents, in my view, is that General Cermak has the title of commander of the Knin Garrison, and he exercises various powers as we have seen over the past days in relation to his position of garrison commander, whereby he also deals with matters that go beyond what is stipulated in the regulations as being the duties of a garrison commander. D609 shows that the staff for hygiene and sanitation measures in Knin is subordinated to General Cermak, which is coherent with what we saw in the earlier document, the report about the dispatching of the clearing teams to the various parts of Croatia, whereby the Ministry of Interior determined how the teams should be formed, how they should proceed, what regulations they had to apply when, for example, burying human bodies, but the document there also clearly stated that they would operate in coordination and under the authorisation of the military authorities in the area. D609 is, for me, an example of the authority, the military authority in the area has over the clearing teams, whereby as I said General Cermak can issue orders to the head of the staff for hygiene and sanitation measures in Knin. The last document we saw, it uses the word "request," and I understand the confusion that sometimes "request" is used in documents where actually one would say from the contents it is an order, but the last document, obviously it is not an order, and I draw that conclusion from the context of the documents. General Cermak can request the Ministry of Interior to provide additional staff, but I see that as a -- a question he asks to provide -- excuse me, to the Ministry of Interior to provide him with personnel, whereby it's the Ministry of Interior who will decide whether or not he receives the personnel. I mean, and the other requests we have seen from the context, we could see that it is a superior who indeed requests a subordinate to do something, but from the contents it was basically the superior ordering the subordinate to do something. I think when looking at these documents, one has to look at who signed it, for whom is it intended, what are the de jure or de facto relations between the sender and the addressee, and based on those aspects we can -- and the contents of the document, we can determine its significance in the sense of whether it's a request in the sense of a question or a request in the sense of an order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Let us turn now to the document you referred to earlier, Exhibit P496, which shows the order of the 11th of August, issued by General Gotovina based on the Cervenko order of the 5th of August, 1995. And in the aim of clearing up the terrain this order is made. We see a clear-up operations in Knin, and then we see a detachment command. We've taken a little time going through this because this all comes together now, these names we've seen before which the Court may recognise. Mr. -- Captain Radovic, Mr. Davidovic, Mr. Batur. Turning to page 2. Again further names there, what's to happen in relation to the composition of the groups. Page 3. Again referring to Captain Radovic as the clear-up coordinator, equipment. Page 4. Reference to Dr. Brkic's guidance that we've looked at right at the start.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you point out the name of Dr. Brkic in the document because I haven't seen it yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, at the top of the page you see 15/10/93. That's the guidance we looked at the start, Dr. Brkic's guidance. Yes?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have it on my screen, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have a look at -- apparently you're referring to the date, the date of the 1993 document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, it may be on the previous page, Your Honour. I know e-court has its marvels, but documents are -- go down, please.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There we fine it at the semi-last line, the 15th of October, 1993, which is the date of --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But I was thinking of Dr. Brkic in the context of his role in Knin, as we saw by the documents by -- I mean his reports to General Cermak. I haven't seen his name in this document, but maybe I missed something.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You haven't seen his name here at all, and we'll look up. That's why I pointed out to you in Mr. Cemerin's report of the 8th of August his announcement that he was going in, as opposed to being ordered by the civil protection staff. And we're going to look further as to what he says about himself. This is all from General Gotovina, an organisation for dealing with this matter. We see on the last page that it's dispatched to the various parts of the Split Military District including the garrison commander.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Very well. That's already an exhibit. If we go to the next document, 65 ter 4981. This is a report to General Cermak from Colonel Brkic again. It's dated the 12th of August. Report about hygiene and sanitary measures. It repeats that earlier report that we saw that he filed on the 9th, giving the details on the first page, citing again his guidance of the 15th of October. If we go to page 2. He refers to further details there about the marking of the graves. Oh, it's page 1 of the one on e-court. And we can see that he refers to how the graves are marked at a proper distance, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, may this document be made an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D1059, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1059 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Kay, earlier, and I do understand that it's a more complex matter, our attention was drawn to the numbering of documents and the dates, 5th of August, et cetera. I noticed looking at some of these documents that at least apart from other evidence about who arrived by what date, that there seems to be little consistency in the numbering of documents and the dates. For example, here we have a 02 document of the 12th of August, where we have already on the 8th and 9th, we have far higher numbers. Just for me to understand the position of the Defence, is that through the other evidence we have -- we would have to conclude that one document of the 5th of August could not have been issued on the 5th of August, not primarily on the basis of the numbering but, rather, on the basis of the other reference. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, so there's no mystery, I'll put my case and explain it to the Court. I think it's proper as you're --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but if I understood your position well, then we don't have to repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you say, No, you have misunderstood the position, then, of course, I would ask you for a clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. That -- that order of the 5th of August was impossible for General Cermak to have been issuing on that day. He wasn't in Knin. He didn't have that -- that stamp. Our case on this is that Dr. Brkic turned up, said he was -- made himself available to General Cermak and started doing his business which General Cermak allowed him to do, and then he came back to General Cermak saying he needed an order and got him to sign the order. That's our case, and you will have seen from the other documents that there was some controversy about what Dr. Brkic was doing in Knin when the other organs were already in work, and a deputy minister had become involved sending him down there. So it's a picture of chaos and confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so the dates on the documents and the position of the Defence is explained by the need at a later date to have some form of document. That's clear to me now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. And it was Dr. Brkic justifying himself is our case, Your Honour, in relation to these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for this explanation. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry that there was mystery about it, but I didn't want to comment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but, of course, I'm looking at the numbers --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- in relation to the dates, and then, of course, I'm asking myself how to understand matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Let's move now to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps to finish that open issue with D marked for identification 1057, if we go to 65 ter 5387, then we see that the correct original B/C/S is uploaded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You it's now -- the correct one is uploaded?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'll check that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you, Mr. Waespi. 2D07-0372.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is a report from Dr. Brkic to the Minister of Defence, Mr. Susak, on Knin garrison paper. It's a report on his work between the 5th and 12th of August, 1995, and he's writing to the minister, although not in response to any particular order or request from the front of the letter here. We'll look down further to see what's said. "Dear Mr. Minister, I came to liberated Knin on 5th of August, 1995, to a regular inspection that I perform on occasions like this, and I found the situation as following ..." And then he gives an account in this report. We can note that it's in conflict with the account given in Mr. Cemerin's document of the 8th of August, but he says that there was a problem in the cemetery. There was a big hole. There were several bodies in the hole, several more around it. It wasn't done properly, "so I issued an order to an engineer, Jelic, to treat the bodies in accordance with the Geneva Convention, to perform a complete forensic processing - identification," burial of each body, mark the graves, and contacted the local priest. All activities had to be minimised because the president visited on the 6th of August. He went back on the 7th of August in the morning and saw that the hole behind the church had been buried. He inquired, "But I did not get the answer. It became clear to me that because the task was so sensitive and because I had other tasks, my presence there had been necessary." And then he refers to that order from General Cermak stating he formed the company who took over the task, and together with civil protection, performed the task in accordance with all the rules about the hygiene and situation, i.e., bodies that were in the same room were separated and buried separately. And he refers to further details there. He refers to animal sanitation. And you can see just before the conclusion of the letter: "I hope I have justified my presence," and he refers to another doctor. Had you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have this included in footnote 980 on English page 246, second part of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And there we are. We brought it to the attention the Court. It exhibits the order that we've looked at already, as well as some further appended documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May this document be made an exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D1060, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1060 is admitted into evidence, and D1057 is also admitted into evidence, the original having been uploaded. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The next document is 2D07-0428. This time dated the 14th of August. Again from Dr. Brkic, this time to the chief of the Main Staff, General Cervenko, and report about his participation in operation Summer 1995. I don't need to go into the details of that, but it's just there for completeness as to what he is writing about. May this document be made an exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D1061, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And the next document is Exhibit P543. It's similar but not identical to the report that we saw was made to the minister of defence, Mr. Susak, earlier. It's from Dr. Brkic to General Gotovina, dated the 16th of August, reporting on his activities between the 5th, 12th of August, and it opens: "General, sir, came to liberated Knin on the 5th of August, 1995, to a regular inspection that I perform on occasions like this, and I found the situation as following," and then that information we've seen before as well as the rest of the letter is the same as the letter to the minister. Just moving on from that, there is another report that we need to see. Exhibit D612. This time Dr. Brkic is writing to the chief of staff, General Cervenko, on the 29th of August, and reporting on clearing up the terrain between the 5th, the 28th of August. And again he repeats: "That's something I do after any such action," and then goes into the detail of his work and what he could see at the cemetery. If we could turn to page 2. The further details we've already seen in the earlier reports. Further detail, however, on the 7th of August. "...I came to the graveyard to find the hole filled up... who did that? Got no reply. It became clear to me that my presence was essential." A team was formed, and he refers to the order, and then we know there's further detail there, clearing up the terrain. And at page 3 about the final work that will be in a report to be sent giving further technical details.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. There's no further information I need to point out in relation to that, but that's Dr. Brkic's role. And now we will go to that involving the Ministry of the Interior and what takes place there. Your Honour, if we can go to Exhibit D232. This is a document from the assistant minister at the Ministry of Interior called Mr. Zidovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know what Mr. Zidovic's position, what his responsibility is in the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we look at the end of the document, we will find it, but I have no specific knowledge of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: He's in charge of the civil protection and fire service and issues a whole series of orders to the police administration departments with that responsibility. And we can see here on this page, on the 4th of August, orders that are given there. Page 2, paragraph 3, referring to the Zadar-Knin police administration amongst others, telling them to prepare the activation of units. Immediately activated a detachment for hygiene and sanitation measures and a detachment for clearing up the terrain. Paragraph 4: "In the said police administrations in cooperation with the military authorities and on their approval, engage in the removal of the bodies of the dead, in cooperation with the criminal police. Keep records," et cetera. If we go to Exhibit D233, we an order the next day, the 5th of August, and I'm going to take matters very swiftly thereafter to conclude the whole series of documents that have already gone into evidence, Your Honour, and just deal with the matter globally, as I believe the Court is well seized of these exhibits now. 5th of August here, we see hygiene and sanitation measures. This document again is from Mr. Zidovec. It's estimated that there is a large number of bodies of people who were killed in the area. Promptly engage all available resources on the ground. Get manpower from other administrations. Page 2, part of the steps to be taken concerning dead bodies and explosives, examining the area. Identifying, photographing, fingerprinting the body. Identification number, and buried in single graves properly marked with a cross, and saying only single graves shall be dug. Under international law any grave containing more than four bodies is considered a mass grave. Page 3. Recording that dead bodies shall be recorded on forms, an example of which is attached. And then giving details of units to be carrying out this task. Mr. Theunens, are you familiar with these documents emanating from the Ministry of Interior and further such documents all sent to the Zadar-Knin police administration, to other police administrations, as well as Kotar-Knin police administration on measures and steps to be taken in relation to the sanitation and clearing of the terrain?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with these specific documents, but I'm familiar with the procedure and also the cooperation and the role of the military authorities in the implementation of these procedures.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you aware of the role of the civilian authorities in the implementation of these procedures?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We've had countless, probably 20 or 30, exhibits in this case detailing this, none of which are, in fact, referenced to General Cermak. They show, in fact, the Ministry of Interior operating independently and separately under their own procedures in relation to this matter. Did you appreciate that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I wouldn't look at these documents in isolation from -- from, for example, the instruction you showed earlier where it was clearly stated on the first page that these activities have to be carried out in cooperation and under the authority of the military authorities. The document we see now, I mean -- no, D232, clearly state in paragraph 4 that there is a requirement for cooperation with the military authorities, and I think from a common-sense point of view, that is logical. In an area where military operations are conducted or have been conduct, the military is the best organised structure. They know the terrain. They may know where bodies are. They may know where, for example, booby-traps or explosives are. And even if the Civil Defence carries out the specific activities, they will have to cooperate with the military authorities and receive instructions from the military authorities as to where and when they can carry out the sanitation activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: These very detailed orders to identified units within the civil protection of the department of the ministry of interior show, in fact, that General Cermak is not in command of these agencies in Knin; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have seen a number of documents including those signed by Brigadier Brkic where reference is made to a command of General Cermak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, we've seen that, but we've looked at the military documents, and if you like, we can go through the 30 or 40 of Ministry of Interior documents all setting out the procedures which you say you're familiar with which show the Ministry of Interior operating within its own hierarchy and not viewing itself as being subordinated to General Cermak; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you that it's not the subordination of the Ministry of Interior to General Cermak, but it is the operation of elements of the Ministry of Interior, i.e., Civil Defence units operating in cooperation and under authority of the military authorities in the specific area, and for what the Knin Garrison area is concerned the documents I have included in my report on pages 245 and 246, indicate that General Cermak is the military authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You are completely overstating your argument on this matter, aren't you, Mr. Theunens? You have cited solely in the part of your report dealing with the garrison and General Cermak, the Brkic orders; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: They're actually reports by Brigadier Brkic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is also P05 -- we already had P506, there may be discussion about the date, but it was signed by General Cermak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Let's just focus on the question. We're dealing now with the Ministry of Interior. We have established that the Ministry of Interior has a civil protection department. Civil protection department is issuing orders to the police administrations who have civil protection units within them, correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Those units are then operating under the orders of the civil protection departments of the police administrations, and they are dealing with the issue of the hygiene and sanitation of the terrain. And I can refer -- well, to 30 or 40 orders. The Court has seen them. Those -- those operations are acting entirely without the authority of General Cermak commanding them. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I explained, it is the Ministry of Interior that instructs teams to be sent. It also explains the teams how they are to carry out their work, but it is the military authority that determines when, where these activities have to be carried out, and it is also the military authority, at least based on the documents I have reviewed and include in my report, who receive information on the implementation of the sanitation tasks. The teams will obviously also report or send information on the implementation of their duties to the Ministry of Interior as well as, for example, as you showed, on problems they have, but again, it is not an exclusively Ministry of Interior type of activity. There needs to be cooperation with the military authorities, and as we saw in the first, call it, generic document you showed, the activities of the sanitation are carried out in cooperation and under the authority of the military authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You mentioned cooperation, but you say cooperation under the authority of the military authorities. Putting Brkic on one side, which is the person not from the civil protection department, but within the Ministry of Interior civil protection department where is there a single order from General Cermak commanding them?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there are two elements in the question. What --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just answer -- it's clear what I'm getting at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay -- Mr. Theunens, you can point at two elements in the question, but would you please identify them, and then I'll tell you whether you can address them, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the first element is that Mr. Kay states that I said cooperation under the authority. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the second element was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The second element is orders by General Cermak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's first deal with the first one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first one, I don't have the exhibit number, but the -- what I call the generic document we saw stated that sanitation activities had to be carry out in cooperation with and under the authority of the military authorities. That was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Having clarified this, could you please move to the second element of the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The -- the second element, well, I have the document P506 in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can we call that up, please. Exhibit P506.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the one where there's discuss about the date or the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That's the Brkic document. No, you're ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I think part of the question was that leave apart Dr. Brkic, if there were any orders apart from him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, this is an order by General Cermak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, I'm afraid we're going to have to go through the exhibits then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I'm afraid, Mr. Theunens, you're playing this for one side alone. You are.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I can only draw conclusions on the documents I have seen. Now, the only, I mean, option -- other option I can see is that also in addition to this team, and we also have then the team established -- or the team establish by General Gotovina, that there are separate teams operating, i.e., what you call Ministry of Interior teams, but then I would have to review more documents of the Ministry of Interior to see also to whom these Ministry of Interior teams send information in relation to their activities. We saw a document this morning, even this review of the activities of the teams, of the Civil Defence teams, where the communication problems in Knin were highlighted, and it was specifically highlighted that there were -- that they couldn't even reach General Cermak in Knin. We only saw the document on the screen, but I don't remember seeing any reference to another senior member of the arm forces in that document. Now, if -- if the situation is that there are separate teams, separate Civil Defence teams, operating in the area, I have not seen documents, such documents or documents indicating that during the preparation of my report, but I'm willing to consider such documents, and then obviously review what is included in the report. What is included in the report is based on the material I reviewed, and there we have an order by General Cermak to establish a team or to -- excuse me, to establish a staff, what we see now, P506, and we have the Brkic reports. I have not come across material that --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You will be, after the break.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It's --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I just want to say the position of Mr. Brkic, indeed you show a document from the Civil Defence where certain reservations are made about the position or the role of Mr. Brkic. I would expect the members of the Civil Defence to highlight that issue also with General Cermak. It's speculation, I agree, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's not speculate.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will have a break, and we'll resume at 11.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Shall we go back to Exhibit P496, please, General Gotovina's order of the 11th of August. And my questions, Mr. Theunens, actually concern Mr. Cermak's authority, which is at the section of the report that we are -- are dealing with. And this is the order that you have referred to several times, dated the 11th of August. We can see that the order is to establish operative groups and that there is a detachment command, and you'll see Captain Boris Radovic. He worked for the MUP Ministry of Interior as well, civil protection department. I'm sorry, Boris Davidovic did, the deputy clear-up coordinator. I don't know whether I read that out correctly or rightly. And we see Stanko Batur, who was had he of the civil department -- civil protection department, in fact, of Zadar-Knin police administration and various other members of the detachment command. If we go to page 2, we see the further names there and what each operations group should consist of. If we go to page 3, in the middle of the page we see the time and place at which parties are to report shall be determined by the clear-up coordinator, Captain Radovic. And we can see the various equipment from the logistics bases and operation groups of the brigades in paragraph 5. We see a combination in 6 relating to personnel and equipment from the police -- from the Split-Dalmatia Police Administration, and that the clear-up is to be, in line 10, with that guidance of the 15th of October, 1993. If we go to the next page, and it's paragraph 12: "Dispatch daily reports by 2200 hours, indicating the situation of 2000 hours; the reports shall be dispatched to the OPL sector of the Croatian Army Main Staff." And a final report no later. And this document is sent to various parts of the Split Military District, including the Knin Garrison. Now, the issue I was asking you about was Mr. Cermak, whether he was in command of the Ministry of Interior Staff or even the Split Military District Staff involved with this clear-up of the terrain, and you'll notice that the order of general Gotovina causes that the reports be submitted to the army Main Staff; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that -- I mean the sending to the army of the Main Staff, I agree, but that's the second component of the question. The first component is that this order does not make any reference to a role by General Cermak in relation to these clearing teams, particularly the clearing team for Knin, and I find that unusual. When I addressed the role of General Cermak in the context of clearing of the terrain, that is the section on the pages 245 and 246, I have included his orders for the establishment of a terrain hygiene and sanitation measures staff. I have tried when reviewing the documents to make a connection between these two documents, i.e., between P506. There's also D610 which is an order by General Cermak, and P496, and I wasn't able to make such a connection except that P496 is actually issued after P506, even if there is -- there can be debate about the date P506, but D610 is dated the 10th of August. And just to finish the answer, we have the reports by Brigadier Brkic to General Cermak at least one or two reports dated the 12th of August. That is all I can say in connection to your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Now, just looking at this and then looking at what this document can tell us, that under this order of the Split Military District, the reporting system was not to General Cermak; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Which indicates that General Cermak was not in command of this particular order and operation.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I mentioned, P496 does not mention a role for General Cermak. He's only mentioned as one of the addressees.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, could you answer the question. You're meant to be an expert on command and control, because one of the essentials of the command and control would be to have a reporting system to General Cermak if he was in command of these units; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Command and control indeed implies also a verification of the implementation of the order. The most logical manner is that, indeed, one receives reports, but as I mentioned it several times, the commander also has to collect information himself. Now, I agree with you that the most logical approach would have been to -- if General Cermak had a role in relation to the teams established by P496, the most logical approach would have been to mention his name in connection to the Knin team, determine what his role was, and then also depending on his role, determine in P496 whether or not he was to receive reports. That is not done in P496.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And the documents of General Cermak that you refer to indicate his involvement in a capacity before this date, before this period when he issues an order and Dr. Brkic reports to him about matters before this date.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The orders by General Cermak I have reviewed are indeed before this date, but as I mentioned, there are -- is at least one report by Brigadier Brkic from after this order. What I have in footnote 980 is a report by Brigadier Brkic dated the 12th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And the events in at that report are before the 11th of August; isn't that right? We've looked at it today.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The title is "Report about hygiene and sanitary measures taken --"

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We'll look at it. We'll look at it.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we could maybe see the previous page of P496 to see whether there is a date established in the order indicating when the order enters into effect. I mean, just to clarify the question of Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't understand. I don't understand you.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Often an order will also include an information as to when the order is to come into effect. We have seen many orders which stated this orders comes into effect immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It says "hereby." It says "hereby."

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And it says: "Dispatch daily reports by 2200." So it's to come into effect straight away. And if we go to 65 ter 4981, it has an exhibit number now, but I --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. You have D1059?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I haven't got the number. Yes, 1059, which is dated the 12th of August. You will see that, in fact, it goes up to events on the 11th of August.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. Again this is not exact science, but one would expect that Brigadier Brkic, if the teams established by the order of General Gotovina in P496 were already active, had arrived and had start with their activities, that Brigadier Brkic would have informed General Cermak about that. Again, it's not a must, but it would be logical in the context of military reporting and the types of reporting that Brigadier Brkic is sending, but I want to emphasise that this is not a kind of final conclusion, but it -- I just want to highlight that it would be illogical for Brkic not to mention the teams established by General Gotovina if they had already been active.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. We -- we've seen what Brkic has written and to whom thereafter, and now we're going to look at the Ministry of Interior reports and documents that were issued, because you said you were unaware of them. If we see Exhibit D444. That's D444. This is a document dated the 5th of August, 1995. It's from the assistant minister, Mr. Zidovec again, to the police administration in Zagreb, Operations Staff. It concerns dispatching assistance to the Zadar-Knin Police Administration and Civilian Protection Forces to go there. It's not a document referenced General Cermak in any way, but it is the 5th of August. If we go to Exhibit D447. This is dated the 6th of August, 1995, again from the Assistant Minister Zidovec from the Ministry of Interior to the police administration in the Primorje Gorski Kotar operations staff about dispatching assistance to the Zadar-Knin police administration. We can see the terms of that.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document stated they are to be sent to Gracac to assist with the clearing. Now maybe Gracac is just and assembly point from where they will be dispatched to other areas, but Gracac is not part of this zone covered by the -- at least as it is determined in D33 of the zone covered by the Zadar-Knin garrisons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I know that, Mr. Theunens, but the indictment, as you will recollect, is drafted very differently in this case from the garrison area, and so there are various matters that go outside the garrison area, and it's a matter of evidence in relation to this case. We can see Gracac mentioned there, assisting with the clearing of the terrain of Zadar-Knin police administration. Identifying who they're to report to. Mr. Sacic.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: And that is --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is logical and, I think, coherent with what I have said earlier. That the teams are dispatched and then need to -- have to contact the local authority. I have to discuss the presence of Special Police in the Gracac area at length and also the role of Mr. Sacic, but the teams are sent to the area, and have to contact there the authority, who is going to task them and as to where and when they will carry out the tasks, which in general terms, i.e., the modus operandi has been determined by the Ministry of the Interior as they have to abide by specific procedures while carrying out their tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Exhibit D448. This is another document from the assistant minister Zidovec, dated the 6th of August, 1995, to the Zadar-Knin operations staff of that police administration. Yes?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe this concerns again areas, Korenica -- I'm not sure what would be now, but Korenica and Gracac, outside the zone of responsibility of the Knin Garrison as has been determined in D33.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You have no need to tell us about that. We do know about the Knin Garrison area, and as I said, this is a case involving a wider allegation than the Knin Garrison area. There are matters that I am caused to deal with outside that. Please accept it from me. But it mentions Knin here and Udbina, yes. And it's the mobilisation of 150 members of that Civil Protection Unit, and the Zadar-Knin police administration is ordered to ensure room and board for them. If we go to Exhibit D43. Exhibit D43 is dated the 7th of August, 1995. It's from Assistant Minister Zidovec again, to the Split-Dalmatia operations staff this time. It concerns assistance to the Zadar-Knin police administration. And then going down the scale to Knin again for the needs of a rapid terrain clearance of the town of Knin, urgently mobilise 100 civilian protection conscripts, and they shall be dispatched for jobs. They must report to Mr. Stanko Batur in Knin police station. We recollect him from the 8th of August, report by Mr. Cemerin as well as General Gotovina's order on the 11th of August. And again police administration will be providing transportation, et cetera. If we go to D449, Exhibit D449. This is a document dated the 8th of August, 1995, dispatching assistance to Zadar-Knin police administration again, although it's a Gracac order, and it requires further conscripts. It states the number and what's to happen in terms of uniforms, and it's to the Istria operations staff. If we go to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Kay, you're putting it to the witness. I understood from his earlier answers that he considers these documents not surprising to the extent that it's mainly focusing on making available persons rather than to give any details. If the other documents are the same, then it might not be necessary to go through all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I'm grateful to Your Honour. I'll put the proposition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll know how the expert understands these documents, what -- how he explains that Mr. Cermak is not mentioned or referred to in any way, whereas it's clear to the Chamber that you give a different significance to the absence of any mentioning or reference of Mr. Cermak in these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I haven't dealt with this issue actually explicitly having looked an at these documents. If I might put a question to the witness on it. I won't go through the rest of it as the Court --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As you did now, you introduced the document and didn't ask any questions and went on to the next document, which is, of course, at the certain moment, questions should be put to the witness in relation to them as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, if these people were reporting to the command of General Cermak, he would have been copied in to the order, wouldn't he?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have seen different documents dealing with, as Your Honours explained, the making available people. In one case it was explained they had to contact Mr. Zeljko Sacic, which I then explained why I considered that coherent with what I said earlier. In a later document there was the chief of the Knin police. There are documents which, as I explain, do not deal with the area covered by the Knin Garrison, and I agree with you these documents do not mention General Cermak. That's all I can say about them, because there are different types --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But the question was --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that if these units or these -- yes, if these units would be put at the disposal of General Cermak, whether it would not have been logical or to be expected that he would have copied on these documents. That was the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe there was one document, one mentioning the head of the Knin police administration. It would have been logical, even though the document doesn't explain whether -- I believe it was Mr. Batur, whether he was to contact or not Mr. Cermak in relation to the use of the teams. And that brings us back to the initial discussion, so -- but in a strict sense, these documents do not mention General Cermak. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And if he was to have command, he would have to know what was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was part of your earlier question. The witness apparently has chosen to -- to specifically deal with the matter, which of course is understood by the Chamber in a certain way as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I will skip those other ones, then, sending these people down to the Zadar-Knin police administration, and let us look at D -- Exhibit D464. Have you been familiar with any of those documents we've been producing so far?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think that I had seen them before, except, of course, P496.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is there any reason why this aspect of the case was not analysed by you in your section on the report concerning General Cermak?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reason is that -- or I have not analysed the role of the Civil Defence because I considered it outside the sphere of my experience or expertise, and that's also why you can find that in the -- the small section dealing with the role of General Cermak in relation to clearing of the terrain in Knin, I have not made reference to any Civil Defence documents. I only made reference to orders, i.e., orders issued by General Cermak or documents sent to General Cermak. And that's also what I said before the break, that I had not considered the civilian defence documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. If we look at Exhibit D464, we see again that the assistant minister, Mr. Zidovec, on the 16th of August is sending to all those police administrations -- and just while we're here, the Zadar-Knin police administration, did you know that that was the police administration that was the back-up or resource centre, if you like, for the Kotar-Knin police administration?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, even though I'm not a hundred per cent sure of the municipalities covered by the Zadar-Knin police administration or the Split-Dalmatia police administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It's the structure that Kotar Knin receives resources because it doesn't have these departments from Zadar-Knin which is the controlling police administration. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec is asking for submission of information from the police administrations because they're necessary for compiling reports, and he wants information on the clearing up of bodies, information on number of civilians in reception centres. Again, if part -- if Mr. Cermak was part of the operation for dealing with this matter, surely he would have been requested to provide his information.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not from the military point of view.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We're not looking at a military document. We're looking at the Ministry of Interior document. You have said what you've said about General Cermak being in command and the superior authority, and now we're looking at the system because you also comment on systems of command and control and reporting, and now we're looking at it in action, Mr. Theunens. Surely this would have been something, if he occupied the position you say he did, that he would have been requested to either receive from the police administrations or to have provided information himself.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
